Activities & Experiences
Curated for Melinda & Troy · Potrero, Costa Rica · February 2027

Mel and Troy, you told me you are not the lie on the beach kind, so this is built around that: a welcome sail for everyone, a real answer on the Jurassic Canyon, and the waterfalls, ATVs, chocolate and cooking you asked about. Nothing is booked yet, so read it as a menu. Pick what excites you, and I will shape it into a plan.

01 · Your Welcome Sail

You told me you wanted a welcome boat day rather than a welcome dinner, and I love that. The catch along this coast is that many boats top out at around 20 people. This one takes your whole group on a single catamaran, so nobody is split up on the first day everyone is together.

Thursday 18 or Friday 19 February · Before Your Wedding
SAILING FROM TAMARINDO OR FLAMINGO
Your Welcome Catamaran
The whole boat to yourselves, an open bar, lunch on board, and the Pacific at its best.
Capacity
One boat for up to 75, your whole group sails together
Sunset sail
1:30pm until just after sunset, about 5 hours
Morning sail
8:00am to 12:00pm, about 4 hours
On board
Open bar with tropical drinks, beer and wine, lunch prepared by the crew
In the water
Snorkel gear for a swim stop
Out there
Dolphins and sea turtles, and February is humpback whale season on this coast
Why this one
  • It is the welcome you described: everyone together, relaxed, on the water
  • One boat for the whole group, which very few operators here can do
  • The boat is yours alone, so it runs to your timing, your music and your toasts
  • Nothing for your guests to organise, they just turn up and step on board
  • The sail home at sunset is the best hour of the day out here

My recommendation, the sunset sail on the Thursday. It leaves Friday free for travel days and last arrivals, and gives everyone a full day to recover before the wedding.

02 · The Jurassic Canyon

The Jurassic Canyon is real, and it is as good as it looks. It is also not in Guanacaste: it sits in Bajos del Toro, in the mountains in the middle of the country, about five hours from Tamarindo. As a day trip from the coast it does not work. As part of a few days in Arenal, it absolutely does.

BAJOS DEL TORO · CENTRAL MOUNTAINS
The Jurassic Canyon
Waterfalls on every side, an emerald river, and a canyon that really does look like the film.
The hike
About 11 km round trip, 4 to 6 hours
The terrain
A steep descent and the same climb out, river crossings up to the waist, rock scrambling
Guide
Required, it crosses protected land, so it runs with local guides only
Best for
Fit adults, 14 and over, happy in cold mountain water
Timing
February is the dry season, the best window of the year
Distance
About 1 to 1.5 hours from La Fortuna (Arenal)
Why build a trip around it
  • It is the one thing you brought to me, and it deserves a proper plan
  • From Arenal it becomes an easy morning drive instead of a ten hour round trip
  • Arenal gives everyone else plenty to do on the same day, so the group splits and comes back together for dinner
  • Coming the week before, as you mentioned, this is exactly the kind of trip that brings a group together

An honest note, this is a day for the adventurous half of your group rather than all forty. The descent, the cold water and the climb back out will sort that out on their own, and that is fine. I am confirming with the guides how many people they can take in one day.

Pricing
Group rate being confirmed with the guides this week. I will send it the moment I have it.
03 · A Few Days in Arenal

There are two easy ways to do it. You can land and head straight to Arenal for two nights or more, then come down to the coast for the wedding week. Or you can start on the coast and go up for two nights. Either way you are back in time for the welcome sail. Arenal is the volcano and rainforest side of Costa Rica, with hot springs, hanging bridges and great food, so it is a completely different few days from the beach.

Day 1 · Into ArenalLand in Liberia and drive up, or come up from the coast, with a swim stop at Llanos de Cortés waterfall on the way · Hot springs in the evening

04 · Waterfalls and Canyons from the Coast

If Arenal is too much, these all give you that turquoise water, canyon and waterfall feeling in a single day from Tamarindo. They are quite different from each other, so I have added who each one is for.

Closest to the Jurassic Canyon
La Leona Waterfall
Wade and swim up a narrow turquoise canyon to a hidden waterfall, then hot springs and volcanic mud. About 2 hours of hiking with river crossings. For the adventurers.
approx. $220 + tax per person
Lunch and transport included · Pickup from Tamarindo, Flamingo or Potrero being confirmed
The most beautiful
Sensoria Reserve
A private reserve near Rincón de la Vieja: a guided trail past waterfalls and impossibly blue pools, then a pool fed by a thermal river. Lots of steps, gentle pace. For the whole group.
Rate being confirmed
Full day · About 2 to 2.5 hours from Tamarindo or Flamingo
The iconic one
Río Celeste
The famous sky blue river and waterfall, a farm visit with sloths and frogs, and a swim at Llanos de Cortés on the way back. A long, rewarding day.
approx. $140 + tax per person
Lunch and pickup from the Tamarindo and Flamingo area included · About 12 hours
Best for a big group
Rincón de la Vieja National Park
A volcano trail past steaming vents and bubbling mud, a swim at a waterfall, lunch, then ten hot spring pools and a mud bath. Moderate 2 hour hike.
approx. $140 + tax per person
Lunch and pickup from the Tamarindo and Flamingo area included · About 10 hours
The easy one
Oropéndola Waterfall
The easiest of all: a 10 minute walk to a turquoise pool, a long swim, lunch with a view, then hot springs and mud, all at your own pace.
approx. $305 + tax per person
Door to door transport from Tamarindo or Flamingo included · About 9 hours
For the hikers
Cerro Pelado and La Piedra del Indio
A proper hike up to big views over Guanacaste, then down to a waterfall to cool off. For the walkers in the group.
approx. $190 + tax per person
Lunch and transport included · Pickup from Tamarindo, Flamingo or Potrero being confirmed
All prices are approximate, per person unless noted, and exclude 13% tax · Transport is not included unless a card says so · Final pricing confirmed on booking · Rates shown are group rates for 6 or more

How I would choose, for the canyon feeling, La Leona. For the most beautiful day with the least effort, Sensoria. For the whole group together with something for everyone, Rincón de la Vieja. And if the famous blue is on your list, Río Celeste.

06 · A Taste of Costa Rica

You mentioned the cooking class you loved in Italy, and chocolate. Here is the hands-on side of Costa Rica: chocolate making, cacao farms, coffee, and the corn kitchen of the Blue Zone.

Hands-on
Bean-to-Bar Chocolate Class
Roast, grind and temper real cacao, then pour and decorate your own bars to take home. A small chocolate factory 5 minutes from Flamingo and 20 to 25 minutes from Tamarindo.
approx. $75 + tax per person
2 hours · Can also be hosted at your villa or venue, a small travel fee applies
Closest to your Italy class
Blue Zone Day: Caves and Corn Kitchen
Explore the limestone caves of Barra Honda, then a traditional ancestral lunch and a hands-on masterclass baking corn snacks in a wood fired clay oven, in Nicoya, one of the world's five Blue Zones.
approx. $220 + tax per person
Transport included · Pickup from Tamarindo, Flamingo or Potrero being confirmed
Farm visit
On the way to Arenal
Cacao Farm Morning
Walk the cacao orchards near Bijagua: harvesting, fermentation and drying, seasonal fruit tasting, then a farm lunch. Guided in Spanish. Pairs beautifully with a Río Celeste day, same town.
approx. $65 + tax per person
4 hours · 2.5 to 3 hours from the coast, transport quoted separately
Farm visit
On the way to Arenal
Farm Picnic on Horseback
Ride through cacao fields and forest trails, swim in natural river pools, then a rustic picnic and a cacao tasting at the farm. Minimum 5 people, book 30 days ahead.
approx. $235 + tax per person
4 hours · 2.5 to 3 hours from the coast, transport quoted separately
